activation.claim: This file specifies required future capture; it does not attest that capture exists or is complete.
required_before_p1t: Mac and VPS capture daemons are installed and continuously healthy
one immutable content store, retention horizon, and authentication policy are frozen
host signing public keys and key identifiers are frozen
a destructive-write, truncation, restart, offline-gap, and sequence-conflict acceptance test passes on both hosts
a public target-blind readiness receipt binds daemon, policy, key, content-store, and acceptance-test digests
currently_unset: Mac and VPS signing key identifiers
immutable content-store locator and retention attestation
activation.transition_rule: A target-blind pre-P1 protocol commit may set executable true only after every required readiness artifact exists. P1T may not precede that commit.

origin.meaning: Who or what produced or controls the delivered bytes.

exposure.meaning: Whether an authenticated delivery path to a participant or model is proved.

orthogonality: Every evidence unit receives exactly one origin and exactly one exposure class.
No origin value implies an exposure value.
Copied or generated bytes inherit neither origin nor exposure from their container.
Tool origin is not sufficient for MACHINE_REGISTRY_CONTACT.
Authenticated-upstream origin is not sufficient for IMMUTABLE_SOURCE_CUSTODY after rendering.

capture.delivery_definition: Bytes count as delivered when they are rendered or returned to a frozen human participant, language model, agent context, tool consumer, or generated-artifact consumer. Merely existing on a public platform is not delivery.

host_journals.content_rule: Every delivered byte stream is copied to the immutable content store before or atomically with delivery. Truncation, replacement, deletion, and abandoned partial writes receive signed records.
host_journals.chain_rule: Each host uses a strictly monotonic sequence and binds the exact preceding receipt; restarts continue the chain and boot identity is recorded.
host_journals.offline_rule: Research and benchmark delivery are forbidden while the local capture daemon is unhealthy. Work performed during an unproved interval invalidates the protocol.

session_capture.rule: Capture append increments, offsets, truncations, and final bytes from every frozen participant/model session endpoint on both hosts; periodic endpoint scans are reconciliation only and cannot cure a journal gap.

required_properties: versioning or write-once retention through the fixed horizon and audit period
no raw semantic bytes in public Actions logs or artifacts

required_sources.complete_when: Git object, ancestry, ref-source, and tree receipts authenticate the frozen interval; any bytes rendered beyond the bounded machine lane also have a signed delivery-journal record.

Each explicit root is authenticated and every overlay byte actually delivered to a participant/model is present in a signed host journal and immutable content store; files never delivered are not semantic exposure merely by storage.
The frozen Mac signing key verifies one unbroken sequence from P1T through cutoff, every referenced blob exists, and all frozen Mac delivery endpoints reconcile to the chain.
The frozen VPS signing key verifies one unbroken sequence from P1T through cutoff, every referenced blob exists, and all frozen VPS delivery endpoints reconcile to the chain.
An authenticated inventory proves every journal-referenced object exists with exact bytes and frozen retention; the locator, authentication, and retention fields are non-null before P1T.

Every owned-platform byte stream crossing a frozen delivery endpoint is captured before rendering or publication and reconciles with signed host receipts; global platform state is not claimed complete.
The pre-invocation declaration, producer receipt, output object, and signed delivery receipt agree; an undeclared delivered output is UNKNOWN and fails closed.

explicit_non_sources.reason: Global public availability is not semantic delivery, and complete deleted or transient external-platform history cannot be authenticated by this project. Any such bytes actually rendered to a participant/model are captured by the host delivery journal.
Recursive archival of every Actions log is not an exposure boundary. Only output bytes delivered to a participant/model or declared generated consumer enter the delivery journals.
Storage outside an explicit research root is not exposure. Use of such a path for benchmark research or delivery is an unjournaled channel and fails closed.

forbidden_omissions: A delivered byte stream may not be omitted because another source appears to duplicate it.
A delivered byte stream may not be omitted because it is believed not to contain a future identity.
An identity-only output may not be omitted after delivery to a human or language model.
Deleted, overwritten, expired, truncated, or inaccessible delivered evidence creates a coverage gap unless an earlier signed content-addressed capture proves the exact bytes.
A participant or model may not use an unregistered host, browser, chat, tool, repository, or generated-output channel during the interval.
Endpoint inventories, Git mirrors, API snapshots, and best-effort sync cannot cure a missing signed journal interval.
